subject: TiltAI Dedicated: hardware guidance — memory vs token throughput
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Harper <jamie@tiltai.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: TiltAI Dedicated: hardware guidance — memory vs token throughput

Jamie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, you asked for a concise recommendation on which GPU mix to reserve for the TiltAI Dedicated commitment (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given your two dominant workloads:

- Long-context assistant sessions (avg context 64k tokens, peak 128k) — latency-sensitive, memory-bound.
- High-throughput embedding/batch ranking (short contexts, high QPS) — throughput/cost-sensitive.

High level recommendation (summary):
- Memory-first reserve: H100-heavy pool for long-context stateful inference (pin KV cache, fewer replicas).
- Throughput-first reserve: L4-heavy pool for stateless short inference + embeddings with autoscaled A100 for mid-range models.

Attached is an initial sizing matrix that maps expected concurrent sessions -> SKU mix and rough token-cost delta. Key callouts inside the sheet:
- When >60% of committed capacity is long-context, H100 yields ~30–45% reduction in tail latency and significantly fewer OOMs vs A100.
- For mixed workloads under budget pressure, a hybrid pool (H100 for 20% of slots + L4 for bulk) gives predictable SLAs and lowest blended cost.

Next steps:
1) Can you share a 2-week sample of request profiles (size distribution, QPS by route)? I included a quick template (tiltai-metrics-sample.json).
2) If comfortable, we can model three purchase trims (latency-first, balanced, cost-first) and show cost/latency tradeoffs under your contract horizon.

Thanks — attaching the matrix.

[Attachment: h100_vs_a100_l4_fitting.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)]
[Attachment: tiltai-metrics-sample.json (json, 14KB)]

— Ben

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 15:42 Jamie Harper <jamie@tiltai.ai> wrote:
> Ben —
> Appreciate the quick summary and the matrix. A couple of clarifying questions before we send the sample:
> 1) For the H100 recommendation, are you assuming 80GB training variants or the 94GB configurations? Our models currently use a 70–85GB working set after quantization.
> 2) We run a mix of stateful sessions and stateless inference behind feature flags. If we start with a 20% H100 carveout, how painful is autoscaling between pools when long-context load spikes?

Great questions — answers below: 

1) H100 sizing assumption: the matrix uses the 80GB SXM-like memory profile as the baseline (post-quantization working set 70–85GB fits with conservative KV cache headroom). If you regularly hit >90GB working sets we should evaluate 94GB-class configs (or add an H100 slot buffer).

2) Autoscaling/fallthrough behavior:
- Short answer: cross-pool autoscale and graceful fallthrough are supported but require configuration.
- Implementation notes: 
  - We recommend a primary-first routing policy: prefer same-pool routing (reduces cold-cache OOMs) and configure an overflow policy that routes to a compatible model variant (smaller context window) on L4/A100 for non-critical requests.
  - For stateful sessions, we recommend pinning active sessions to H100 for duration of session; for burst protection use a hot-standby H100 buffer (10–20% of H100 pool) rather than shifting sessions mid-flight.

Cost/latency tradeoff examples (in-sheet):
- 20% H100 carveout: +12% reserved spend vs all-L4, but long-context P95 latency improves by ~40% and session failure drops to <1%.
- 40% H100 carveout: +26% reserved spend vs all-L4, near-zero long-context OOM events; recommended for latency SLAs <300ms P95.

I can run a tailored three-trim model once you share the sample. Priyom — can you confirm whether a 10% hot-standby H100 buffer is operationally sane for our ops team and if we should recommend an A100 fallback pool instead of L4 for certain model families?

— Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jamie Harper <jamie@tiltai.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 18:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TiltAI Dedicated: hardware guidance — memory vs token throughput

Ben / Jamie —

Quick ops input:

- 10% hot-standby H100 is reasonable for a first commit; it keeps headroom for long-context bursts and simplifies routing (we avoid frequent cross-pool session migrations).
- If TiltAI expects predictable sustained long-context concurrency >150 sessions, recommend sizing additional H100s rather than relying on A100 fallback. A100 can be a fallback for degraded latency scenarios, but you'll see higher tail latency and increased engineering complexity handling partial KV cache hits.
- L4 is excellent for high QPS stateless workloads; use it as the primary pool for embeddings, cheap chat completions, and reranking. For models that require mixed precision and moderate memory (~40–60GB), A100 is a cost-effective middle ground.

Operational checklist for the proposal:
- Define two routing policies in the Dedicated config: 
  1) stateful-primary (pin to H100 for session lifetime)
  2) stateless-fast (prefer L4, fallback A100 then H100 for special cases)
- Add a test phase in the first 30 days to monitor OOM events and P95 latency per route.
- Add a clause in the purchase SOW for a 30-day adjustment window to re-allocate reserved slots if behavioral mix diverges >20% from projections.

Happy to join a walkthrough with TiltAI next week. Ben / Kimberly — if you want, I can prepare a short ops slide that maps the sheet to the routing/policy config.

— Priyom
